description: Supply-chain policy for ronl-business-api. Companion to .github/zizmor.yml
and the Supply-chain audit workflow: zizmor enforces that every action
reference is a commit digest, Renovate keeps those digests current. Pinning
without automated updates decays into an unpatched tree, which is worse
than floating. See SECURITY-PIPELINE.md.
baseBranchPatterns targets acc, this repository's integration and default
branch. main is promoted from acc and must never receive dependency pull
requests directly.
prConcurrentLimit 5 is a sized cap, and what sizes it here is REVIEWER
ATTENTION as much as Static Web Apps staging environments. The three acc
SWA workflows carry paths: filters on pull_request as well as push, and
none of them watches the root lockfile or package.json, so lock-file
maintenance and root-only updates claim no preview (#134 ran none). A
dependency pull request that edits a workspace package.json does: one
under packages/pa-cockpit/** or packages/shared/** holds a preview on both
frontend-acc and pa-demo-acc at once, as #140, #141, #147 and #149 did.
All three acc apps are on the Standard plan, 10 environments each (read
from Azure on 2026-09-15); frontend-acc was Free, 3, when five pull
requests exhausted it on 2026-08-28. Five Renovate pull requests holding
two previews each would still leave room on Standard.
Lock-file maintenance is exempt from this cap and from prHourlyLimit; its
packageRule below says why.
Security advisories bypass the cooldown. Without this override the
14-day wait would delay exactly the updates that must not wait, which
is why such policies get disabled mid-incident. Requires GitHub
Dependabot ALERTS to be enabled on the repository; Dependabot security
UPDATES must stay off, or it opens competing PRs that ignore the cooldown.
dependencyDashboardApproval is set false here explicitly, because major
updates below need approval: a security fix that happens to be a major
version must not wait on a checkbox.
Actions land across all ten workflows at once, so they are grouped
separately from the workspace dependencies below.
Azure/static-web-apps-deploy publishes v1 as BOTH a 2021 tag
(1a947af9992250f3bc2e68ad0754c0b0c11566c9) and a 2024 branch head
(4d27395796ac319302594769cfe812bd207490b1). The workflows pin the
branch head; Renovate's github-tags datasource resolves the tag, so it
would open a routine-looking digest update that reverts nine deploy
steps to 3.5-year-old code. minimumReleaseAge gives no protection - the
target commit is years old. Re-resolve by hand if this action ever
needs to move. See SECURITY-PIPELINE.md.
Four deployables, four groups. An update that breaks one workspace
should not be entangled with the others in a single pull request -
each has its own deploy workflow and its own acceptance site.
There are six packages but only four groups: pa-cockpit is
private: true and compiled into both frontend and pa-demo, and shared
feeds both frontend and backend. Neither deploys on its own, so an
update under either stays ungrouped and arrives as its own pull
request - which is also the honest shape, because it is the one case
that redeploys two sites at once.
matchUpdateTypes lists every update type EXCEPT lockFileMaintenance.
Without it these rules stamp a group name onto lock-file maintenance
too, and one refresh arrives as several identical pull requests with
byte-identical lockfiles, multiplying its share of prConcurrentLimit.
Its own default is groupName null. Learned in linked-data-explorer
(#92, #93, #94); see linked-data-explorer#97.
Major updates wait in the Dependency Dashboard (#16) as checkboxes and
hold no slot in prConcurrentLimit until someone ticks one. This is what
replaces the global dependencyDashboardApproval that governed every
update until now (#20, superseded): that key was set during adoption so
Renovate raised nothing while the same workflow files were being pinned
by hand on a branch. That race ended when pinning finished, but removing
the key outright would release the whole queue at once.
The queue is why the replacement is scoped to majors rather than dropped
entirely: of 35 entries pending approval on 2026-09-12, all but four are
majors - express 5, react 19, typescript 7, vite 8, jest 30, eslint 10,
tailwindcss 4, node 24, postgres 18 - which nobody merges on autopilot
anyway. Behind this rule they stay checkboxes; the four genuine
minor/patch updates flow normally under the 14-day cooldown.
Below 1.0.0 a minor bump is a major in all but name: semver gives 0.x
no compatibility promise, but Renovate classifies 0.4 -> 0.5 as minor,
so the rule above lets it through. On 2026-09-14 that opened #138,
eslint-plugin-react-refresh ^0.4.5 -> ^0.5.5, whose 0.5.0 requires
ESLint 9 and flat config; every workspace here is on ESLint 8 with
.eslintrc.cjs, so audit, both previews and the lockfile update failed
on ERESOLVE. Such updates now wait as dashboard checkboxes too.
matchCurrentVersion is checked against the locked version when the
manifest holds a range (CurrentVersionMatcher,
lib/util/package-rules/current-version.ts), so ^0.4.5 locked at 0.4.26
matches. Patch updates stay routine. Security fixes still bypass this:
vulnerabilityAlerts sets dependencyDashboardApproval false.
Lock-file maintenance is the ONLY thing that moves the transitive tree.
Nothing had refreshed this one before 2026-09-12, when the first
authenticated Semgrep scan found 435 findings, 419 of them Supply Chain
(249 reachable) across 1266 npm dependencies. In linked-data-explorer a
single refresh closed 63 of 66 Supply Chain findings with no manifest
change, which is why triaging those findings before a refresh would be
work thrown away.
prConcurrentLimit 0 and prHourlyLimit 0 exempt THIS branch from both
limits; every other update keeps the repository-wide 5 and 2. Renovate
computes a branch's limit from the upgrades inside it and treats 0 as
no limit (calcLimit, lib/workers/global/limits.ts), and this branch holds
exactly one upgrade, so nothing else inherits the exemption.
Needed because the first scheduled run, on 2026-09-14, was rate-limited
and opened nothing. An earlier version of this comment said holding
majors behind approval would keep a slot free. It could not: the
concurrent count includes every open Renovate PR, security PRs included
- only the CHECK is skipped for them - so seven open security PRs alone
exceeded the limit of 5 before any routine update was counted.
prPriority 10 still orders it first among branches eligible in the same
run. If a Monday is missed anyway, tick its box under Rate-Limited on the
Dependency Dashboard (#16): a dashboard check bypasses the limits.
See linked-data-explorer#97.
engines is a floor we set, not a version to chase. rangeStrategy bump
above rewrites it to the newest release: on 2026-09-14 #144 moved
engines.node from >=22 to >=22.23.2 and #145 moved engines.npm from
>=10.0.0 to >=10.9.9, a floor that no Node 22 release satisfies
(22.23.2 bundles npm 10.9.8). Nothing enforces engines here -- no
engine-strict, and deps:check does not read it -- so a raised floor only
turns every install on a slightly older toolchain into EBADENGINE noise,
and the root drifts from packages/backend and from App Service's
NODE|22-lts. widen leaves a range untouched when the new version already
satisfies it (npm versioning getNewValue: >=22 stays >=22), so Renovate
has nothing to raise. The exact runtime lives in .nvmrc, which stays
maintained.
minimumReleaseAge repeats the top-level 14 days and changes nothing:
Semgrep's renovate-missing-minimum-release-age flags any rule matching
on matchDepTypes that does not set it locally, whatever the top level
says.
